request: Analyze GSE110507 for the paper (Overexpression of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) induces skeletal muscle hypertrophy): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

accessions: GSE110507 (not named in the paper; rat VDR-OE RNA-seq, S2.7.p1)
GSE47881 (human 20-wk RET microarray, S2.8.p1; separate series, not this case)
final.assay: rat tibialis anterior RNA-seq (Illumina HiSeq 4000, 75 bp PE), Rsubread featureCounts
final.primary_estimand: Effect of in vivo electrotransfer VDR overexpression (pCAGGS-mVDR, right TA) vs contralateral empty-vector control (left TA) on rat TA gene expression, paired within animal, n = 7 (S2.7.p1, FIG1, FIG5). No exercise intervention in the rat experiment.
planned_contrasts: VDR-OE vs contralateral empty-vector control, paired by animal (S3.2.p1; paper: 3,330 genes at P < 0.05)
final.exercise_component: Human 20-week resistance exercise training (pre vs post) is analysed only as VDR mRNA correlations with lean-mass/1-RM change, using GSE47881 (S2.8.p1, S3.4.p1, FIG7); not in GSE110507.
final.paper_method: edgeR: CPM filter at a count of 10, TMM, glmFit with design accounting for animal pairing (S2.7.p1)
final.paper_results: 3,330 genes P < 0.05; 310 gene-sets FDR < 5%, ECM up, tRNA aminoacylation/mTOR down (S3.2.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The paper's RNA-seq (S2.7.p1, S3.2.p1) compares VDR-OE TA with the contralateral empty-vector TA in 7 rats; it is a genetic gain-of-function experiment with no exercise. The only exercise data are the human RET microarrays from GSE47881 (S2.8.p1), used for VDR correlation (S3.4.p1). The paper does not cite GSE110507.

final.owned_subset: 14 VDR knock-in samples (animals 416-422); the 14 VDR knock-out (shRNA) samples (animals 423-429) are not part of this paper
checks: rat TA, IVE, pCAGGS-mVDR right vs empty pCAGGS left (treatment_protocol_ch1) matches S2.2/S3.1
HiSeq 4000, TruSeq, 7 animals per arm match S2.7.p1 and FIG1 n = 7
GEO contact Iain Gallagher = IJG, who did the bioinformatics (S5.p1)

ownership.reasoning: The paper names no accession for the rat RNA-seq, but GSE110507's protocol, platform, tissue, group size and contact author all match; the series also deposits a VDR knock-down arm not reported here.

alignment.reasoning: raw_tar merge names columns by GSM id; exact match to the metadata index (inspect: 28/28). Animal id gives the pairing key; vdr status gives arm and limb.

matrix.reasoning: All values integer (fraction 1.0), max 3.17e6; GEO description: raw RNA-seq derived counts per gene (Ensembl 89); paper used Rsubread feature counts into edgeR (S2.7.p1).

design.subject: subject
design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: GSE110507 contains only VDR overexpression / knock-down vs contralateral control limbs in sedentary rats. The paper's exercise component (human 20-wk RET, pre vs post) is in GSE47881, not this series, so the requested exercise estimand cannot be identified from these data.

candidates.value: vdr OE vs OEctrl paired by subject (paper's RNA-seq contrast)
candidates.reason_rejected: genetic VDR gain-of-function, not exercise; outside the requested exercise estimand
VDR knock-down arm not reported in this paper and not exercise

design.reasoning: The request is how exercise affects gene expression; every sample in GSE110507 is from non-exercised rats differing only by electrotransferred construct. A VDR-OE contrast would answer a different question, so the case is refused at design rather than manufacturing an exercise contrast.

discrepancies.paper: names only GSE47881 (human RET) for transcriptomics
discrepancies.data: GSE110507 is the rat VDR-OE/KD RNA-seq, unnamed in the paper
discrepancies.disposition: recorded; ownership matched on protocol and contact

discrepancies.paper: exercise only in human RET cohort (GSE47881)
discrepancies.disposition: blocks the exercise estimand; refused at design
